endonym.gloss: what is owed on the ground

description.value: A boundary record drummed by a shelf colony across roughly two hectares of plateau floor, in the item-by-item form the colonies use for anything that may be answered. It is repeated at intervals and is admissible, in the shelf sense, at any later drumming.

content.value:
Item: the ground was cleared and not by us. Item: eleven kilometres of it, and nothing standing. Item: we came onto it in the year after and we were first.

Item: nothing was owed on that ground when we came. Item: we have held it eleven years and entered every year of it. Item: the forest returns at the eastern edge, four hundred metres in eleven years.

Item: what returns takes ground from us. Item: the debt for that ground stands against the forest and is entered here. Item: the forest does not answer.

Item: an account that is not answered is not closed. Item: we will drum this again in forty days.
